gaps.note: The 32 client lamps are placed coincident with each channel's Tx/Rx strip. The COUNT and the FUNCTION are datasheet and manual; the POSITION is arrived at by elimination on a photograph - only three features repeat per channel, and the number and the adapter are ruled out - rather than by seeing a lit lamp. The part carries the objection in full, including the two ports on this same face that wear the identical strip with no datasheet LED behind it.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a unit CARRYING TRAFFIC. Every image held shows Power and Status green while every client strip is white, which says the channels are dark, not that the lamps are elsewhere. With light on a few channels, whatever turns green settles it outright.

gaps.note: The rear carries two PSU bays, a fan tray and ETH1-ETH5, and the DCP-M manual's rear figures are of the DCP-M40, a different product with all its management at the back. No photograph or figure of THIS unit's rear exists in the corpus, so the rear view is the chassis envelope and its bays only.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a DCP-M32 rear, or a manual figure that names it as such.

gaps.note: Only front and rear are modelled. 510 deep is stated but nothing in the corpus shows a side, top or bottom of this unit.

channel-plan.note: silkscreen, read off the photograph - D914 to D960.5 on a 150 GHz grid, sixteen per row. NEITHER THE STENCIL NOR THE REQUESTED-PARTS LIST CAN BE TRUSTED HERE: the master prints every number 0.5 high and ends at 961, outside the datasheet's stated plan, and that list transcribes p.24 as "9540/9175/9200/9130", which are misreadings of the same labels. Two sources wrong in different ways is why this comes off the photograph.

client-lamps.note: smartoptics/m32-client-lamp@1, one per channel, coincident with the Tx/Rx strip - THE CAPTION IS THE LAMP. See that part for the count, the manual's behaviour, the elimination argument that places them, and the objection that does not defeat it.

connectors.note: all optical ports are LC. "All optical ports are of LC connector type" (DS FRONT SIDE CONNECTIONS), and UM s13 adds the polish - "Line port(s) LC/UPC connector type". That is a harder statement than the DCP-F family got and it covers all 35 adapters.

front-management.note: UM s3.7 - on this variant the console and ETH0 are on the FRONT, with ETH1 to ETH5 at the rear. The DCP-M40's are all at the rear. So the DCP-2's rear ETH0-over-CONSOLE pair must not be copied onto this device, and fig 2-7 and the quick-turn-up guide's fig 3, which show a DCP-M40 rear, are live traps.

line-and-osc-lamps.note: THE PHOTOGRAPH SETTLES THE COUNTS THE DATASHEET LEFT OPEN, differently for each. The OSC port has TWO round lamps, between a printed "Tx" on their left and "Rx" on their right - visible as two unlit lenses, so common/led-dot@1 twice. The Line port has ONE white strip, identical to a client channel's, so it takes the same part the channels do. Both were unmodelled while the count was open; neither is now. The 1510 and 1625 OTDR ports carry the same strip and get NO lamp: the datasheet's VISUAL INDICATORS block names an LED for the clients, the Line and the OSC and names none for those two, so their strips are drawn as printed decor.

method.note: FACT SHEET FIRST, THEN THE ARTWORK - working/intake/factsheets/dcp-m32-cso-zr.md. The inventory and every count came from so-ds-dcp-m32-cso-zr-r1.2 and the DCP-M User Manual before any drawing was opened.

photo-calibration.note: THE MEASUREMENT FRAME FOR EVERYTHING BELOW, and it is derived rather than assumed. The vendor photograph is 2.1082 px/mm with the face's x=0 at pixel 60.40 and y=0 at pixel 321.5. That comes from a least-squares fit of the sixteen upper Tx/Rx strip centres against the stencil's connection points, run separately on the ten strips left of the mid-face gap and the six right of it: BOTH halves return 2.1082 px/mm to four figures, which is what makes the scale trustworthy, and the half that also agrees with the ETH0/RS232 and OSC-cage connection points to 0.2mm fixes the origin. The unit in the photograph HAS NO RACK EARS - it is a bare chassis on white - so the 440 body is the whole of the dark plate, and thresholding that plate's edge is what the earlier 2.1318 px/mm came from: it overshoots by six pixels on the left and three on the right where the edge is soft. An independent check falls out of the fit rather than into it: the Line port's lone strip measures 13.28 against a part that is 13.2 wide.

port-positions.note: FROM THE PHOTOGRAPH, and it disagrees with the stencil in one specific place. Under the calibration above the eight upper channel-pair midpoints sit on a 30.83 pitch to better than 0.1mm, seven times running, with one wider gap in the middle of the face. The stencil's connection points agree with the photograph to 0.1mm for the three pairs RIGHT of that gap and are 5.1mm to the right of it for the five pairs left of it - because the stencil draws the mid-face gap 36.5 wide where the unit has 41.7. Everything else in the frame - the ETH0/RS232 jack centre at 15.0, the OSC cage centre at 35.0 - lands on the stencil's cps to 0.2mm. So the photograph is not mis-scaled; the drawing has one block in the wrong place, and the photograph is taken for all 35 adapters so that the face is internally consistent.

power.note: datasheet POWER CONSUMPTION. Recorded on the contract rather than inferred from the chassis, which is a different product.

rows.note: FROM THE PHOTOGRAPH. Each channel block carries a white Tx/Rx strip above the upper adapters and below the lower ones; the 1510/OTDR/Line group has ONE strip, at the upper position, and bare plate beneath. Rows measured: upper labels baseline 5.5, upper strips 6.5, upper adapters 10.4, lower adapters 23.4, lower strips 36.0, lower labels baseline 40.8.

size.note: datasheet - so-ds-dcp-m32-cso-zr-r1.2, "Size (WxDxH) 440mm x 510mm x 1RU", 13 kg. NOT TRANSPOSED, unlike the DCP-404's and the DCP-F-A22's, whose labels are: here the labels and values are in the printed order, confirmed three ways - the ordering line spells out "1RU, 19in, D=510mm", UM s13 gives labelled WIDTH/DEPTH/HEIGHT rows, and the DCP-M-DE manual gives a sibling in the same shell 45mm (H) as a number. THE DEPTH IS 510, NOT THE DCP-2's 500 and not the DCP-R's 505. A requested-parts list says "same 440x45x505 family shell - chassis dims can be reused"; that is wrong and the datasheet is right.

stencil-defects.note: SIX now, in one master, which is why nothing here is taken from it unchecked. The channel numbers print 0.5 high and run past the datasheet's plan; one caption reads "Rx Rx" where every other reads "Rx Tx"; the hex vent field is drawn as six cells; the 1510, OTDR and Line adapters are drawn in the LOWER row where the unit has them in the upper; those first two are drawn 13-16mm from where they sit and NOT abutting, where the unit abuts them as one pair; and the mid-face gap is 5.2mm narrow.

vent-fields.note: three hex fields on the front, all photo-measured: an L-shaped one over the left block notched around the OSC lamps and cage, a two-column one in the mid-face gap, and a one-column one hard against the right edge. Each is a lighter backing rect with the library's vent pattern painted over it, because the pattern draws only its holes and a vent field on a plate this dark is otherwise invisible. The 62mm between the last channel and the right-hand field is bare plate on the real unit, not an omission.
